transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brought you in to see me?

Yeah, hey, thanks. Um, well, I guess what brought me in is that things just got really, really intense lately, and my boss actually kind of suggested I come talk to somebody. 

See, I work landscaping, right? And normally, I’m just a regular crew guy. I show up, I run the mowers, I lay the mulch, I do whatever the foreman says, and I go home. I've been doing it since high school, so I know my lane. But recently, I just... I went from being a normal crew guy to suddenly trying to run, like, three massive commercial bids all at the exact same time. And I'm not even in the office! I don't do the paperwork. But I was calling up city people, like tracking down their direct office numbers from the municipal website, trying to pitch them on this huge public park renovation idea I came up with. 

I was on the phone constantly, lining up wholesale plant suppliers from out of state, getting quotes on bulk shipments of hardscaping stuff we don't even use. And I was messaging literally everybody I knew about this park idea. I mean everybody—my boss, my coworkers, friends, guys I haven't even talked to in five years. I was just blowing up their phones with all these plans and blueprints I was drawing up on my lunch breaks. It was like... I don't know, it was like I just couldn’t shut it off. I had to get all these projects off the ground right that second, and I just couldn't stop pushing and pushing it.
Have you been using any drugs or substances—like cocaine, amphetamines, or other stimulants—recently?

No, no, definitely not. I mean, I totally get why you’re asking that, because honestly, looking back at how I was acting with all those phone calls and blueprints, I probably looked exactly like I was on something. And, you know, in landscaping, it’s no secret that some guys, especially on the temporary crews, they’ll mess around with uppers or whatever just to get through those brutal fourteen-hour summer shifts when you’re hauling stone in ninety-degree heat. You see it happen. But that’s never been my thing. I don't touch any of that. 

I mean, I’ll grab a Red Bull or a Monster from the gas station if we’ve got a really early morning start, or maybe drink a couple cups of coffee, but cocaine? Amphetamines? No way. Never. Actually, my boss kind of asked me the exact same thing when he told me I should come see someone. He pulled me aside by the work trucks and was like, "Hey man, are you taking something? Because you are bouncing off the walls right now." But I swear to you, I wasn't. I haven't taken anything at all. It was just... it was all just my own brain doing it, just going a million miles an hour all on its own without any help from any drugs or anything like that. I didn't need anything to keep me going, I just naturally couldn't stop.

Have you ever had a period before—lasting a week or more—where you felt unusually low, depressed, or lost interest in things, or on the flip side, felt this same kind of extremely high, energetic, or 'on top of the world' way before now?

Yeah, the low part... man, the low part is really what's been getting me. You asked if it was a week or more, but honestly, it’s way, way more than a week. This... this depression, or whatever you want to call it, it’s been hanging over me for about a year now. Like, a full twelve months of just dragging myself around. 

I remember it really set in last fall, right around when we were doing all the big leaf cleanups and winterizing the commercial irrigation systems. I just started feeling so incredibly heavy, like I had literal paving stones tied to my boots every single day. I'd pull up to my apartment after a shift and just sit in my truck in the driveway for like half an hour, just staring at the steering wheel because I couldn't even summon the energy to pull the door handle and walk inside. And it just stayed like that. Through the winter, into the spring... just this constant, heavy fog where I didn't care about anything. I stopped wanting to grab a beer with the crew, stopped caring about fixing up my truck, just wanted to lay in the dark. 

But then... well, then I had that whole crazy period I just told you about, with the blueprints and the phone calls and feeling like I could take on the world. But right after that stopped? I crashed. And this latest crash... I mean, it is absolutely the worst it has ever gotten. I've never felt this low in my entire life. It’s like I burned up every single drop of fuel I had in my body trying to pitch that park idea, and now I'm just totally, completely empty. I can barely even look at my phone now, let alone call a supplier. It’s just been a whole year of this dark cloud hanging around, but this crash right now, it's just crushing me completely.
How long did that period of feeling extremely energetic, unstoppable, and full of ideas last—was it more like a few days, or did it go on for a week or longer?

Well, the really fired-up, overconfident stretch... the part where I was totally remaking myself for that park pitch and calling everyone under the sun? That lasted about two weeks. Yeah, right around two solid weeks of just going non-stop. 

I remember exactly how it started, too. It was a Tuesday, and we were out at this corporate office park laying down some fresh sod, and it just hit me like a lightning bolt. I started thinking about the layout of this city park near my place, and how inefficient the walkways were, and how they were using the wrong kind of drought-resistant shrubs for this climate zone. And suddenly, I wasn't just thinking about it—I was, like, possessed by it. By Wednesday morning, I was waking up at 3:00 AM, pacing around my apartment, sketching out these massive redesigns on printer paper. I didn't even feel tired. I felt like I had tapped into this secret energy source that nobody else knew about. 

And for those whole two weeks, it was just... escalating. Every day I was adding more to the plan. I was convinced I was going to revolutionize municipal landscaping. I was talking faster, moving faster, eating lunch standing up by the woodchipper while I was on hold with the city planning office. I felt totally unstoppable, like I was the smartest guy in the room and everyone else was just moving in slow motion. My boss kept trying to give me my regular assignments, like pruning the hedges at the bank, and I’d just brush him off like, "I don't have time for hedges, man, I'm negotiating a bulk rate on retaining wall blocks with a guy in Ohio." 

It just kept going and going like that, every single day, weekend included. I think I slept maybe eight hours total across those fourteen days. But I didn't care. I felt amazing. Until, you know... until I didn't. Right at the end of that second week, it was like someone just pulled the plug straight out of the wall. The energy just vanished overnight, and that's when I crashed into this horrible low I'm in now. But yeah, that whole high-energy phase, the unstoppable part, that was a full two weeks.

During this current low period, have you experienced anything like hearing voices, seeing things others don't see, or having thoughts or beliefs that others might consider unusual or not based in reality?

No, no, nothing like that. I mean, I know things have been really dark lately, and I've been feeling like I'm moving through wet concrete, but my mind is still... well, it's still rooted in the real world, you know? I'm not hearing any voices or seeing things that aren't there. 

I actually had a buddy a few years back, this guy I used to work with doing hardscaping out in the suburbs, and he started talking about how the government was tracking him through the radio in his truck. Like, he actually pulled the whole stereo system out of his dashboard one afternoon while we were supposed to be laying a patio, just left a bunch of wires hanging out everywhere. And he'd say he could hear them whispering to him when the wind blew through the trees. It was really sad, honestly, and it got to the point where he couldn't work anymore. But I've never experienced anything even close to that. 

Even when I was going a million miles an hour with the park plans, I knew what I was doing. I mean, the ideas were huge, and I was definitely acting crazy, but I wasn't, like, hallucinating. I wasn't getting secret messages from the TV or anything. And now, being this low... it's just a heavy, crushing sadness. It's not weird thoughts or voices. It's just me, sitting in my apartment, staring at the wall, knowing exactly how miserable I am and knowing that the wall is just a wall. There's no trick to it, my brain isn't playing games with me like that. It's just... it's just this awful, heavy reality. So yeah, definitely no voices or visions or anything like that. Just the depression.
